\section{Introduction}

\subsection{Motivation}

A \emph{projection-valued measure} (PVM) with finitely many outcomes on $\R^n$ is a family of
matrices that are idempotent, pairwise orthogonal, and sum to the identity. It is the algebraic
skeleton of an ideal measurement: the channels are exclusive and exhaustive, and each channel
selects a subspace of state space. The definition is a conjunction of \emph{polynomial
identities}, and polynomial identities are brittle: a real device satisfies them approximately at
best.

There are two standard responses. One replaces sharp projections by positive operator-valued
measures, weakening the algebra. The other keeps the algebra and treats the error statistically,
outside the formalism. This paper explores a third response, available because the hyperreal field
$\Rs$ has room \emph{inside the number system} for a scale of error that is nonzero yet below
every real threshold: keep the identities, but require them only modulo infinitesimals.

The hyperreals form an ordered field properly extending $\R$ and containing infinitesimals ---
nonzero elements $\varepsilon$ with $|\varepsilon| < 1/k$ for every positive integer $k$ --- and
infinite elements such as $\omega = 1/\varepsilon$, whose absolute value exceeds every integer. A
hyperreal is \emph{finite} if it is not infinite. Each finite hyperreal $x$ is infinitely close to
a unique real number $\st(x)$, its \emph{standard part}; we adopt the convention that $\st$ is
extended by $0$ on infinite elements, so that it is a total function $\Rs \to \R$, well behaved
precisely on the finite part.

The question addressed here: \emph{which of the algebraic identities defining a measurement
survive the passage $\Rs \to \R$ given by $\st$, and under what hypotheses?}

\subsection{Summary of results}

Throughout, $n$ and $m$ are finite, matrices are $n\times n$, and channels are indexed by a finite
set $\iota$ of size $m$.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Descent} (Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}). For a finite-entry family, $(\st(P_a))_a$ is a
      PVM if and only if approximate exclusivity and approximate completeness hold.
\item \textbf{Redundancy} (Theorem~\ref{thm:redundancy}). Approximate idempotency is implied by
      the other two hypotheses; the hypothesis list is minimal.
\item \textbf{Sharpness} (Theorems~\ref{thm:sharp1} and~\ref{thm:sharp2}). Both directions fail if
      entries may be infinite.
\item \textbf{Quantization} (Theorem~\ref{thm:quant}, Corollary~\ref{cor:quant}) and
      \textbf{geometry} (Theorem~\ref{thm:internal}).
\item \textbf{Functional calculus} (Theorem~\ref{thm:polycalc},
      Corollary~\ref{cor:annihilator}).
\item \textbf{Coarse-graining and spectral collapse}
      (Theorems~\ref{thm:coarse} and~\ref{thm:collapse}).
\item \textbf{Surjectivity, fibres, strictness, rigidity}
      (Theorems~\ref{thm:surj}--\ref{thm:uniquelift}).
\item \textbf{Entropy} (Theorems~\ref{thm:entropy}--\ref{thm:entropyiff}).
\end{itemize}

\section{The observation map}

\subsection{Scalars}

Write $\Fin(\Rs)$ for the set of finite hyperreals; it is a subring of $\Rs$, and the
infinitesimals form a maximal ideal in it.

\begin{lemma}[Standard part on finite elements]\label{lem:scalar}
For finite $x,y \in \Rs$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x$ is infinitesimal $\iff$ $x$ is finite and $\st(x)=0$;
\item $\st(x+y)=\st(x)+\st(y)$ and $\st(xy)=\st(x)\st(y)$, hence $\st(x-y)=\st(x)-\st(y)$;
\item $x-y$ is infinitesimal $\iff$ $\st(x)=\st(y)$;
\item a finite sum of finite hyperreals is finite, and
      $\st\!\big(\sum_{i\in s}f(i)\big)=\sum_{i\in s}\st(f(i))$ for a finite index set $s$ with
      each $f(i)$ finite;
\item if $x$ is infinitesimal and $y$ is finite, then $xy$ is infinitesimal.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Items (1) and (2) are the defining properties of the standard part, the latter being the statement
that $\st : \Fin(\Rs)\to\R$ is the quotient by the ideal of infinitesimals. Item (3) is (1)
applied to $x-y$. Item (4) is induction on $|s|$ using (2). Item (5) follows from (2):
$\st(xy)=0\cdot\st(y)=0$, and $xy$ is finite.
\end{proof}

The failure of (2) for infinite arguments drives every counterexample below:
$\st(\omega\cdot\omega^{-1})=1\ne 0=\st(\omega)\st(\omega^{-1})$.

\subsection{Matrices}

\begin{definition}
For $A \in \Mn(\Rs)$:
$\st(A) \in \Mn(\R)$ is defined by $\st(A)_{ij} := \st(A_{ij})$ (the \emph{observation} of $A$);
$A$ has \emph{finite entries} if no $A_{ij}$ is infinite; $A$ is \emph{infinitesimal} if every
$A_{ij}$ is infinitesimal; and $A \approx B$ means that $A-B$ is infinitesimal.
\end{definition}

The finite-entry matrices are closed under addition, negation and multiplication --- the last
because a product entry is a finite sum of products of finite hyperreals --- and contain $0$, $I$
and every infinitesimal matrix.

\begin{theorem}[Observation is a ring-like homomorphism]\label{thm:hom}
For $A,B \in \Mn(\Rs)$ with finite entries, and any finite family $(P_a)$ of finite-entry
matrices,
\[
\st(A+B)=\st(A)+\st(B), \quad \st(A-B)=\st(A)-\st(B), \quad \st(AB)=\st(A)\st(B),
\]
\[
\st\Big(\sum_a P_a\Big)=\sum_a\st(P_a), \quad \st(0)=0,\quad \st(I)=I,\quad
\st(A^{\T})=\st(A)^{\T}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Everything is entrywise. Multiplicativity is the only non-formal item:
$(AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$ is a finite sum of products of finite hyperreals, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar}(4) moves $\st$ inside the sum and Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar}(2) inside each
product.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Observation detects the infinitesimal halo]\label{prop:halo}
Let $A,B$ have finite entries. Then $A$ is infinitesimal iff $\st(A)=0$, and $A\approx B$ iff
$\st(A)=\st(B)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Entrywise application of Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar}(1) and (3).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Approximate symmetry descends]\label{prop:symm}
If $A$ has finite entries and $A^{\T}\approx A$, then $\st(A)$ is symmetric.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\st(A)^{\T}=\st(A^{\T})=\st(A)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:hom} and Proposition~\ref{prop:halo}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Entrywise versus operator-theoretic infinitesimality}

Call $v\in(\Rs)^n$ \emph{finite} if each coordinate is.

\begin{theorem}[Entrywise $=$ operator-theoretic]\label{thm:opnorm}
$A \in \Mn(\Rs)$ is entrywise infinitesimal if and only if $Av$ is an infinitesimal vector for
every finite hyperreal vector $v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Rightarrow$) $(Av)_i=\sum_k A_{ik}v_k$ is a finite sum of (infinitesimal)$\times$(finite),
hence infinitesimal by Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar}(5) and (4). ($\Leftarrow$) Apply the hypothesis to
the standard basis vector $e_j$, which is finite; then $(Ae_j)_i = A_{ij}$.
\end{proof}

Thus ``entrywise infinitesimal'' is intrinsic: it says that $A$ has infinitesimal operator norm.
In finite dimensions all norms are equivalent, and Theorem~\ref{thm:opnorm} is the
non-Archimedean shadow of that fact.

\section{The Descent Theorem}

\begin{definition}
A family $Q:\iota\to\Mn(\R)$ is a \emph{projection-valued measure} (PVM) if
\[
Q_aQ_a=Q_a\ (\forall a), \qquad Q_aQ_b=0\ (a\ne b), \qquad \sum_a Q_a = I .
\]
A family $P:\iota\to\Mn(\Rs)$ is an \emph{approximate hyperreal PVM} if
\begin{align*}
&\text{(F) each } P_a \text{ has finite entries};\\
&\text{(O) } P_aP_b \text{ is infinitesimal for } a\ne b;\\
&\text{(C) } \textstyle\sum_a P_a \approx I .
\end{align*}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Descent Theorem]\label{thm:descent}
Let $P:\iota\to\Mn(\Rs)$ satisfy \textnormal{(F)}. Then $\big(\st(P_a)\big)_{a\in\iota}$ is a PVM
if and only if \textnormal{(O)} and \textnormal{(C)} hold. Equivalently, $P$ is an approximate
hyperreal PVM if and only if its observation is a PVM.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Leftarrow$) Write $Q_a:=\st(P_a)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:hom} and Proposition~\ref{prop:halo},
(O) gives $Q_aQ_b=\st(P_aP_b)=0$ for $a\ne b$, and (C) gives
$\sum_a Q_a=\st(\sum_a P_a)=\st(I)=I$. Idempotency then follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:idemfree}.
($\Rightarrow$) If $(Q_a)$ is a PVM, then $\st(P_aP_b)=Q_aQ_b=0$ for $a\ne b$ and $P_aP_b$ has
finite entries, so it is infinitesimal by Proposition~\ref{prop:halo}; similarly
$\st(\sum_a P_a)=I=\st(I)$ gives $\sum_a P_a\approx I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Idempotency is free, real version]\label{lem:idemfree}
If $Q:\iota\to\Mn(\R)$ satisfies $Q_aQ_b=0$ for $a\ne b$ and $\sum_a Q_a=I$, then $Q_aQ_a=Q_a$
for every $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$Q_a=Q_aI=Q_a\sum_b Q_b=\sum_b Q_aQ_b=Q_aQ_a$, all cross terms vanishing.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Redundancy of approximate idempotency]\label{thm:redundancy}
If $P$ satisfies \textnormal{(F)}, \textnormal{(O)}, \textnormal{(C)}, then $P_aP_a\approx P_a$
for every $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:descent} the observation is a PVM, so
$\st(P_aP_a)=\st(P_a)^2=\st(P_a)$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:halo} converts this into
$P_aP_a\approx P_a$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Minimality]
Neither (O) nor (C) is implied by the other together with (F). With $\iota$ a singleton, $P_1=2I$
satisfies (F) and (O) vacuously but not (C). With $|\iota|=2$ and $P_1=P_2=\tfrac12 I$, (F) and
(C) hold but $P_1P_2=\tfrac14 I$ is not infinitesimal.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Sharpness of the finiteness hypothesis}

\begin{theorem}[Failure of ``if'' without \textnormal{(F)}]\label{thm:sharp1}
There is a family $P:\{1,2\}\to M_2(\Rs)$ with $P_aP_b=0$ \emph{exactly} for $a\ne b$ and
$P_1+P_2=I$ \emph{exactly}, whose observation is not a PVM.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put
\[
P_1=\begin{pmatrix} 2 & \omega\\ -2\omega^{-1} & -1\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_2=I-P_1 .
\]
Using $\omega\omega^{-1}=1$, one computes $P_1^2=P_1$: the $(1,1)$ entry is
$4+\omega(-2\omega^{-1})=2$, the $(1,2)$ entry is $2\omega-\omega=\omega$, the $(2,1)$ entry is
$-4\omega^{-1}+2\omega^{-1}=-2\omega^{-1}$, and the $(2,2)$ entry is $-2+1=-1$. Hence
$P_1P_2=P_1-P_1^2=0=P_2P_1$ and $P_1+P_2=I$: an exact hyperreal PVM. But
\[
\st(P_1)=\begin{pmatrix} 2&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
since $\st(\omega)=0$ by the convention on infinite elements and $\st(-2\omega^{-1})=0$ because
$2\omega^{-1}$ is infinitesimal. The $(1,1)$ entry of the square of this matrix is $4\ne 2$, so it
is not idempotent and the observed family is not a PVM.
\end{proof}

The mechanism is transparent: $\omega\cdot(-2\omega^{-1})=-2$ is a finite quantity manufactured
from an infinite entry and an infinitesimal one, and entrywise observation destroys both factors.

\begin{theorem}[Failure of ``only if'' without \textnormal{(F)}]\label{thm:sharp2}
There is a family $P:\{1,2\}\to M_1(\Rs)$ whose observation is a PVM, but with $P_1P_2$ not
infinitesimal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $P_1=(1)$ and $P_2=(\omega)$. Then $\st(P_1)=(1)$, $\st(P_2)=(0)$, which is a PVM on
$\R^1$; but $P_1P_2=(\omega)$ is infinite.
\end{proof}

\section{Dimension quantization and geometry}

\begin{lemma}[Trace of an idempotent]\label{lem:trrank}
If $Q\in\Mn(\R)$ satisfies $Q^2=Q$, then $\tr Q=\rank Q$ as a real number.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The induced endomorphism $T$ of $\R^n$ is idempotent, so
$\R^n=\range(T)\oplus\ker(T)$ and in an adapted basis $T=\mathrm{diag}(1,\dots,1,0,\dots,0)$ with
$\dim\range(T)$ ones. Trace is basis independent.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Dimension quantization]\label{thm:quant}
If $Q:\iota\to\Mn(\R)$ is a PVM, then $\sum_{a}\rank Q_a=n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\sum_a \rank Q_a=\sum_a\tr Q_a=\tr\big(\sum_a Q_a\big)=\tr I=n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Quantized observed weights]\label{cor:quant}
Let $P$ be an approximate hyperreal PVM. Then for each $a$ there is $k_a\in\N$ with $k_a\le n$,
\[
\st(\tr P_a)=k_a=\rank \st(P_a), \qquad \sum_a k_a=n .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\tr P_a$ is a finite sum of finite hyperreals, so $\st(\tr P_a)=\tr\st(P_a)$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar}(4); Theorem~\ref{thm:descent} makes $(\st(P_a))$ a PVM, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:trrank} with Theorem~\ref{thm:quant} finish.
\end{proof}

The hyperreal traces range over a continuum --- anything in the halo of an integer, such as
$1+\varepsilon$ --- while the observed traces are forced onto $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$.

\begin{theorem}[Geometry of observed channels]\label{thm:geometry}
Let $Q$ be a PVM and $V_a:=\range(Q_a)$. Then $Q_av=v$ for $v\in V_a$; $V_a\cap V_b=0$ for
$a\ne b$; $\sum_a V_a=\R^n$; and the family $(V_a)$ is independent in the lattice of subspaces.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
If $v=Q_aw$ then $Q_av=Q_a^2w=v$. If $v\in V_a\cap V_b$ with $a\ne b$, then $Q_av=v$ while
$v=Q_bw$ gives $Q_av=Q_aQ_bw=0$. Spanning: $v=Iv=\sum_a Q_av$ with $Q_av\in V_a$. Independence is
the second argument with $V_b$ replaced by $\sum_{b\ne a}V_b$, every element of which is killed by
$Q_a$ while every element of $V_a$ is fixed by it.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Observation is an internal direct sum decomposition]\label{thm:internal}
For an approximate hyperreal PVM $P$, writing $V_a:=\range\st(P_a)$,
\[
\R^n=\bigoplus_{a\in\iota}V_a, \qquad \sum_a \dim V_a=n .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}, Theorem~\ref{thm:geometry} and Theorem~\ref{thm:quant}.
\end{proof}

\section{Functional calculus}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:pow}
If $A$ has finite entries, so does $A^k$ for every $k\ge0$, and $\st(A^k)=\st(A)^k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Induction on $k$, with base case $\st(I)=I$ and step Theorem~\ref{thm:hom} applied to
$A^{k+1}=A^kA$.
\end{proof}

For a real polynomial $p(X)=\sum_i c_iX^i$ write $p^{*}(A):=\sum_{i=0}^{\deg p}c_iA^i$ for
evaluation at a hyperreal matrix (coefficients coerced into $\Rs$), and $p(M)$ for evaluation at
a real matrix.

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial functional calculus descends]\label{thm:polycalc}
For any real polynomial $p$ and any finite-entry $A\in\Mn(\Rs)$, the matrix $p^{*}(A)$ has finite
entries and $\st\big(p^{*}(A)\big)=p\big(\st(A)\big)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$p^{*}(A)$ is a finite sum of terms $c_iA^i$, each with finite entries by Lemma~\ref{lem:pow}.
Then $\st$ passes through the sum (Theorem~\ref{thm:hom}), through scalar multiplication
(Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar}(2), as $\st(c_i)=c_i$ for a real coefficient), and through the power
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pow}).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Approximate annihilators become exact]\label{cor:annihilator}
If $p$ is a real polynomial, $A$ has finite entries and $p^{*}(A)$ is entrywise infinitesimal,
then $p(\st(A))=0$ exactly.
\end{corollary}

Two instances: $p=X^2-X$ shows that an approximately idempotent finite-entry matrix is observed as
an exact idempotent, and $p=X^2-1$ that an approximate involution is observed as an exact
involution.

\section{Coarse-graining and spectral collapse}

Let $f:\iota\to\kappa$ be a map of finite index sets: a \emph{merging scheme}. Set
\[
(f_*Q)_k := \sum_{a:\,f(a)=k}Q_a, \qquad (f_*P)_k := \sum_{a:\,f(a)=k}P_a .
\]

\begin{theorem}[Coarse-graining preserves the class and commutes with observation]\label{thm:coarse}
\ \begin{enumerate}
\item If $Q$ is a real PVM then so is $f_*Q$.
\item If $P$ has finite entries then so does $(f_*P)_k$, and $\st\big((f_*P)_k\big)=(f_*\st(P))_k$.
\item If $P$ is an approximate hyperreal PVM then so is $f_*P$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1) Expanding the double sum for $k\ne l$ produces only terms $Q_aQ_b$ with $f(a)\ne f(b)$, hence
$a\ne b$, hence $0$; completeness is fibrewise summation; idempotency is then free by
Lemma~\ref{lem:idemfree}. (2) is Theorem~\ref{thm:hom} for a finite sum. (3) combines (1), (2)
and Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Observation of a hyperreal spectral decomposition]\label{thm:spectral}
If $(P_a)$ has finite entries and $(\lambda_a)$ are finite hyperreal scalars, then
\[
\st\Big(\sum_a\lambda_aP_a\Big)=\sum_a\st(\lambda_a)\,\st(P_a).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Spectral collapse]\label{thm:collapse}
Suppose furthermore that there are $f:\iota\to\kappa$ and $\mu:\kappa\to\R$ with
$\st(\lambda_a)=\mu(f(a))$ for all $a$. Then
\[
\st\Big(\sum_a\lambda_aP_a\Big)=\sum_{k\in\kappa}\mu(k)\,\big(f_*\st(P)\big)_k ,
\]
a spectral decomposition over the coarse-grained observed projections; and if $P$ is an
approximate PVM, the coarse family is a PVM.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:spectral} and regroup the sum fibrewise over $\kappa$, factoring $\mu(k)$
out of the $k$-th fibre using $\st(\lambda_a)=\mu(k)$.
\end{proof}

Eigenvalues separated only by an infinitesimal produce a single observed spectral line, whose
projection is the sum of the fine projections: infinitesimal spectral splitting is unobservable in
principle.

\section{Surjectivity, fibres, strictness and rigidity}

Let $\lambda(M)\in\Mn(\Rs)$ denote the canonical \emph{lift} of a real matrix $M$. It has finite
entries, satisfies $\st(\lambda(M))=M$, and $\lambda$ is an injective ring homomorphism.

\begin{theorem}[Observation is surjective]\label{thm:surj}
Every real PVM $Q$ is the observation of an approximate hyperreal PVM, namely of
$(\lambda(Q_a))_a$, which is in fact an exact hyperreal PVM.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Fibres are halos]\label{prop:fibres}
For finite-entry families $P,P'$: $P_a\approx P'_a$ for all $a$ if and only if
$\st(P_a)=\st(P'_a)$ for all $a$. In particular infinitesimally close approximate PVMs have equal
observed ranks channel by channel.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[The approximate class is strictly larger]\label{thm:strict}
The two-channel family
\[
P_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&\varepsilon\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
P_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\]
is an approximate hyperreal PVM observed as the real PVM
$\big(\mathrm{diag}(1,0),\mathrm{diag}(0,1)\big)$, and satisfies $P_1P_2\ne0$ and $P_1+P_2\ne I$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All entries are finite;
$P_1P_2=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&\varepsilon\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is infinitesimal but
nonzero, $P_2P_1=0$, and
$P_1+P_2=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&\varepsilon\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\approx I$ but differs
from $I$. Theorem~\ref{thm:descent} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity]\label{thm:rigidity}
Let $P$ be an approximate hyperreal PVM. Then there is an exact hyperreal PVM $R$ --- satisfying
$R_aR_a=R_a$, $R_aR_b=0$ for $a\ne b$ and $\sum_aR_a=I$ on the nose --- with finite entries, such
that $P_a\approx R_a$ and $\st(R_a)=\st(P_a)$ for all $a$. Explicitly, $R_a=\lambda(\st(P_a))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}, $(\st(P_a))_a$ is a real PVM; by Theorem~\ref{thm:surj} its lift $R$
is an exact hyperreal PVM with finite entries; and $\st(R_a)=\st(P_a)$ gives $P_a\approx R_a$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:halo}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetric rigidity]\label{thm:symmrigid}
If in addition $P_a^{\T}\approx P_a$ for all $a$, the exact model $R$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:rigidity} satisfies $R_a^{\T}=R_a$: an exact orthogonal resolution of the
identity over $\Rs$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness among lifts]\label{thm:uniquelift}
If $Q,Q':\iota\to\Mn(\R)$ satisfy $\lambda(Q_a)\approx\lambda(Q'_a)$ for all $a$, then $Q=Q'$.
\end{theorem}

Thus: observation is a surjection from finite-entry approximate hyperreal PVMs onto real PVMs; its
fibres are exactly the infinitesimal halos; each fibre contains a canonical exact hyperreal PVM,
unique among lifts of real families; and the fibres are non-trivial, containing inexact members.
The approximate world is an infinitesimally thin thickening of the exact world.

\section{The observed Born measure and its entropy}

\begin{definition}
For a real PVM $Q$ and $v\in\R^n$, the \emph{Born weight} of channel $a$ is
$p_a := v^{\T}Q_av$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:born}
If $Q$ is a PVM and $v^{\T}v=1$, then $\sum_a p_a=1$. If in addition each $Q_a$ is symmetric,
then $p_a\ge0$ for all $a$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\sum_a p_a=v^{\T}\big(\sum_aQ_a\big)v=v^{\T}v=1$; and with symmetry and idempotency,
$v^{\T}Q_av=v^{\T}Q_a^{\T}Q_av=\|Q_av\|^2\ge0$.
\end{proof}

Symmetry is load-bearing: for the oblique idempotent
$Q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-3\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $v=(1,1)^{\T}/\sqrt2$ one gets
$p=-1$.

\begin{proposition}[Push-forward]\label{prop:push}
For any merging scheme $f:\iota\to\kappa$, $v^{\T}(f_*Q)_kv=\sum_{a:f(a)=k}p_a$.
\end{proposition}

Let $\eta(t):=-t\log t$ for $t>0$ and $\eta(0):=0$, and define the \emph{observed entropy}
$H(Q,v):=\sum_a\eta(p_a)$.

\begin{lemma}[Scalar engine]\label{lem:engine}
Let $s$ be a finite set, $p:s\to[0,\infty)$ and $S:=\sum_{i\in s}p_i$. Then
$\eta(S)\le\sum_{i\in s}\eta(p_i)$, with strict inequality whenever two distinct indices
$a\ne b$ in $s$ have $p_a,p_b>0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
If $S=0$ both sides vanish. If $S>0$, then $p_i\le S$ gives $\log p_i\le\log S$ for $p_i>0$, so
$-p_i\log S\le\eta(p_i)$, trivially also for $p_i=0$; summing yields
$\eta(S)=-S\log S=\sum_i(-p_i\log S)\le\sum_i\eta(p_i)$. If $p_a,p_b>0$ with $a\ne b$, then
$p_a<S$ strictly, so $\log p_a<\log S$ and the $a$-th inequality is strict.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Entropy monotonicity under coarse-graining]\label{thm:entropy}
Let $Q$ be a PVM with all $Q_a$ symmetric, let $v\in\R^n$ and let $f:\iota\to\kappa$. Then
$H(f_*Q,v)\le H(Q,v)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Regroup $H(Q,v)=\sum_k\sum_{a:f(a)=k}\eta(p_a)$ fibrewise and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:engine} inside
each fibre, using Proposition~\ref{prop:push} to identify the coarse weight with the fibre sum and
Proposition~\ref{prop:born} for nonnegativity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strict loss]\label{thm:entropystrict}
If $a\ne b$ with $f(a)=f(b)$, $p_a>0$ and $p_b>0$, then $H(f_*Q,v)<H(Q,v)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp equality criterion]\label{thm:entropyiff}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:entropy},
\[
H(f_*Q,v)=H(Q,v)\iff \big(\forall a,b:\ f(a)=f(b),\ p_a\ne0,\ p_b\ne0 \implies a=b\big),
\]
i.e.\ equality holds exactly when no two distinct channels of nonzero weight are merged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Leftarrow$) In each fibre either all weights vanish, contributing $\eta(0)=0$ on both sides, or
exactly one weight is nonzero and equals the fibre sum. ($\Rightarrow$) Contrapositive: two
distinct channels of nonzero weight in one fibre have positive weight by
Proposition~\ref{prop:born}, so Theorem~\ref{thm:entropystrict} gives strict inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
If $P$ is an approximate hyperreal PVM whose observed channels are symmetric, then
$H\big(f_*\st(P),v\big)\le H\big(\st(P),v\big)$ for every $v$ and every merging scheme $f$.
\end{corollary}

\section{Algorithms}

The theory is effective when infinitesimals are represented symbolically. Represent a hyperreal
entry as a truncated expression $\sum_{k=-K}^{K}c_k\omega^{k}$ in a formal infinite element
$\omega$. Then the entry is infinite iff $c_k\ne0$ for some $k>0$, infinitesimal iff $c_k=0$ for
all $k\ge0$, and, when finite, its standard part is $c_0$. Observation applies this entrywise at
cost $O(n^2K)$.

The \emph{descent test} for $(P_a)_{a\in\iota}$: verify finiteness of every entry; compute the
symbolic products $P_aP_b$ for $a\ne b$ and check that all coefficients $c_k$ with $k\ge0$
vanish; check the same for $\sum_aP_a-I$; and, if these pass, output the observed PVM, its ranks
and the certificate $\sum_a\rank=n$. Step two dominates, at $O(m^2n^3K)$ field operations. The
exact model of Theorem~\ref{thm:rigidity} is then obtained by observing and re-embedding, at cost
$O(mn^2K)$.

\section{Discussion}

\subsection{What the theory says}

Passing from a non-Archimedean apparatus to what a real observer records:

\emph{Invisible}: infinitesimal cross-talk between channels; an infinitesimal deficit or excess in
total efficiency; infinitesimal spectral splitting; infinitesimal asymmetry; any infinitesimal
failure of a polynomial identity.

\emph{Visible}: everything at finite scale, and --- destructively --- infinite entries, which
break the correspondence in both directions.

\emph{Created by observation}: integrality. Continuum-valued channel traces are snapped to
$\{0,\dots,n\}$, and the observed object is always an internal direct sum decomposition of $\R^n$
with integer dimensions summing to $n$.

Finiteness of the entries is thus not bookkeeping but the substantive content: boundedness of the
instrument's dynamic range, not exactness of its calibration, is what the correspondence requires.

\subsection{Relation to standard viewpoints}

The formalism resembles, but is not, the theory of positive operator-valued measures. There the
algebra is genuinely weakened; here it is kept intact and the field is enlarged instead, so that
exact identities may be satisfied modulo an ideal of infinitesimals. The rigidity theorem shows
these are different moves: an approximate hyperreal PVM is always infinitesimally close to an
exact one, so no new operator-algebraic phenomena appear at observable scale. What is gained is a
calculus of error inside the number system: ``cross-talk is negligible'' becomes an exact
algebraic assertion, and the descent theorem converts it, once and for all, into an exact real
statement. Transfer explains part of this but not all: transfer moves internal first-order
statements between $\R$ and $\Rs$, whereas $\st$ is external, collapsing a whole halo to a point.

\subsection{Limits}

Everything here is finite-dimensional and finitely indexed; Theorem~\ref{thm:opnorm} uses finite
dimensionality essentially, and infinite index sets would require hyperfinite summation. The
observation map is entrywise, which Theorem~\ref{thm:opnorm} justifies in finite dimensions but
which would need an operator-norm formulation in general --- exactly where the compensation
phenomenon of Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp1} would reappear. Finally, the convention $\st(x)=0$ for
infinite $x$ makes $\st$ total but discontinuous; all theorems carry finiteness hypotheses so that
the convention never does mathematical work, and the sharpness examples are precisely the cases
where it would.

\section{Future directions}

\textbf{Definability of observation.} We conjecture that $\st$ on matrices is not first-order
definable in the language of ordered fields with the internal matrix algebra, so that every
theorem here mentioning $\st$ genuinely leaves the internal fragment. The heuristic is that $\st$
collapses the infinitesimal halo to a point, contradicting saturation; the sharpness examples
locate the discontinuity exactly at infinite entries, and rigidity shows every observed statement
has an exact internal model, so the only possible obstruction is definability of the map itself.

\textbf{Infinitesimal spectral gap dichotomy.} We expect a dichotomy for finite-entry hyperreal
symmetric matrices: either all gaps between distinct observed eigenvalues are appreciable, in
which case observed spectral projections are the standard parts of the hyperreal ones channel by
channel; or some gap is infinitesimal, in which case the observed decomposition is strictly
coarser and the fine projections are individually unrecoverable from the shadow. A quantitative
version would be a non-Archimedean analogue of gap-based perturbation estimates.

\textbf{Hyperfinite extensions.} Replacing $\Mn(\Rs)$ by an internal hyperfinite-dimensional
matrix algebra, the descent theorem should persist under uniformly finite operator norm, but the
trace argument would produce hypernatural rather than natural observed weights.

\textbf{Approximate commutant and joint measurement.} If two approximate PVMs approximately
commute channelwise, their observations commute exactly and admit a joint refinement. Quantifying
the converse would connect this circle of ideas to almost-commuting-matrix problems.

\textbf{Non-Archimedean error budgets.} If the slack of an apparatus is $O(\varepsilon^k)$ for
varying $k$, one obtains a filtration of the approximate class. The descent theorem is insensitive
to $k$; finer invariants may not be.

\section{Conclusion}

Under the single hypothesis that no entry is infinite, the entrywise standard part is a ring
homomorphism, so every polynomial identity survives observation. A family of hyperreal matrices is
therefore observed as a projection-valued measure exactly when it is orthogonal up to
infinitesimals and complete up to infinitesimals --- with idempotency coming free --- and the
finiteness hypothesis is sharp in both directions. Beyond the equivalence: observation is
surjective with halos as fibres; every approximate measure is an infinitesimal perturbation of an
exact one, while the approximate class is strictly larger; observed channel weights are quantized
to natural numbers summing to the dimension; the observed decomposition is an internal direct sum;
polynomial functional calculus and coarse-graining commute with observation; infinitesimally
separated eigenvalues fuse; and the observed Born distribution has entropy monotone under merging
with a sharp equality boundary. The algebra of an idealized measurement is robust in the strongest
possible sense against error below the observer's resolution, and fragile only against magnitude
beyond it.

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Number = Fraction | int


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  A computable non-Archimedean field: finite Laurent series in omega
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Hyper:
    """A hyperreal number represented as a finite Laurent series in omega.

    ``coeffs`` maps an integer exponent k to the rational coefficient of
    omega**k.  Positive k contributes an infinite part, k = 0 the appreciable
    part, negative k an infinitesimal part.  Zero coefficients are dropped, so
    the representation is canonical and equality is structural.
    """

    coeffs: Tuple[Tuple[int, Fraction], ...]

    # -- construction -------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def of(d: Dict[int, Number]) -> "Hyper":
        cleaned = {k: Fraction(v) for k, v in d.items() if Fraction(v) != 0}
        return Hyper(tuple(sorted(cleaned.items())))

    @staticmethod
    def real(c: Number) -> "Hyper":
        """The image of a real (here: rational) number in the hyperreals."""
        return Hyper.of({0: c})

    @staticmethod
    def omega(power: int = 1) -> "Hyper":
        """omega**power: infinite for power > 0, infinitesimal for power < 0."""
        return Hyper.of({power: 1})

    # -- ring structure -----------------------------------------------------

    def as_dict(self) -> Dict[int, Fraction]:
        return dict(self.coeffs)

    def __add__(self, other: "Hyper") -> "Hyper":
        out = self.as_dict()
        for k, v in other.coeffs:
            out[k] = out.get(k, Fraction(0)) + v
        return Hyper.of(out)

    def __neg__(self) -> "Hyper":
        return Hyper.of({k: -v for k, v in self.coeffs})

    def __sub__(self, other: "Hyper") -> "Hyper":
        return self + (-other)

    def __mul__(self, other: "Hyper") -> "Hyper":
        out: Dict[int, Fraction] = {}
        for k1, v1 in self.coeffs:
            for k2, v2 in other.coeffs:
                out[k1 + k2] = out.get(k1 + k2, Fraction(0)) + v1 * v2
        return Hyper.of(out)

    # -- non-Archimedean predicates ----------------------------------------

    def is_infinite(self) -> bool:
        """True iff some strictly positive power of omega occurs."""
        return any(k > 0 for k, _ in self.coeffs)

    def is_finite(self) -> bool:
        return not self.is_infinite()

    def is_infinitesimal(self) -> bool:
        """True iff every occurring power of omega is strictly negative."""
        return all(k < 0 for k, _ in self.coeffs)

    def st(self) -> Fraction:
        """Standard part: the constant coefficient (0 on infinite elements)."""
        if self.is_infinite():
            return Fraction(0)
        return dict(self.coeffs).get(0, Fraction(0))

    # -- display ------------------------------------------------------------

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        if not self.coeffs:
            return "0"
        pieces: List[str] = []
        for k, v in sorted(self.coeffs, reverse=True):
            mag = "" if abs(v) == 1 and k != 0 else str(abs(v))
            sign = "-" if v < 0 else ""
            if k == 0:
                pieces.append(f"{v}")
            elif k == 1:
                pieces.append(f"{sign}{mag}w")
            elif k == -1:
                pieces.append(f"{sign}{mag or '1'}/w")
            elif k > 0:
                pieces.append(f"{sign}{mag}w^{k}")
            else:
                pieces.append(f"{sign}{mag or '1'}/w^{-k}")
        return " + ".join(pieces).replace("+ -", "- ")


ZERO = Hyper.real(0)
ONE = Hyper.real(1)
W = Hyper.omega(1)        # an infinite element
EPS = Hyper.omega(-1)     # its reciprocal: an infinitesimal

HMatrix = List[List[Hyper]]
RMatrix = List[List[Fraction]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.  Matrix algebra over the hyperreals and over the rationals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def hyper_matrix(rows: Sequence[Sequence[Hyper]]) -> HMatrix:
    return [list(r) for r in rows]


def h_identity(n: int) -> HMatrix:
    return [[ONE if i == j else ZERO for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]


def h_zero(n: int) -> HMatrix:
    return [[ZERO for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]


def h_add(a: HMatrix, b: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    return [[x + y for x, y in zip(ra, rb)] for ra, rb in zip(a, b)]


def h_sub(a: HMatrix, b: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    return [[x - y for x, y in zip(ra, rb)] for ra, rb in zip(a, b)]


def h_mul(a: HMatrix, b: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    n, m, p = len(a), len(b), len(b[0])
    out = [[ZERO for _ in range(p)] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(p):
            acc = ZERO
            for k in range(m):
                acc = acc + a[i][k] * b[k][j]
            out[i][j] = acc
    return out


def h_smul(c: Hyper, a: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    return [[c * x for x in row] for row in a]


def h_sum(mats: Iterable[HMatrix], n: int) -> HMatrix:
    total = h_zero(n)
    for m in mats:
        total = h_add(total, m)
    return total


def h_trace(a: HMatrix) -> Hyper:
    acc = ZERO
    for i in range(len(a)):
        acc = acc + a[i][i]
    return acc


def has_finite_entries(a: HMatrix) -> bool:
    return all(x.is_finite() for row in a for x in row)


def is_infinitesimal_matrix(a: HMatrix) -> bool:
    return all(x.is_infinitesimal() for row in a for x in row)


def approx_eq(a: HMatrix, b: HMatrix) -> bool:
    """A ~ B: the entrywise difference is infinitesimal."""
    return is_infinitesimal_matrix(h_sub(a, b))


def st_matrix(a: HMatrix) -> RMatrix:
    """The observation map: entrywise standard part."""
    return [[x.st() for x in row] for row in a]


def lift(a: RMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    """The canonical lift of a real matrix into the hyperreals."""
    return [[Hyper.real(x) for x in row] for row in a]


def r_identity(n: int) -> RMatrix:
    return [[Fraction(1) if i == j else Fraction(0) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]


def r_mul(a: RMatrix, b: RMatrix) -> RMatrix:
    n, m, p = len(a), len(b), len(b[0])
    return [[sum((a[i][k] * b[k][j] for k in range(m)), Fraction(0)) for j in range(p)]
            for i in range(n)]


def r_add(a: RMatrix, b: RMatrix) -> RMatrix:
    return [[x + y for x, y in zip(ra, rb)] for ra, rb in zip(a, b)]


def r_zero(n: int) -> RMatrix:
    return [[Fraction(0) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]


def r_trace(a: RMatrix) -> Fraction:
    return sum((a[i][i] for i in range(len(a))), Fraction(0))


def r_rank(a: RMatrix) -> int:
    """Exact rank by Gaussian elimination over the rationals."""
    m = [row[:] for row in a]
    rows, cols = len(m), len(m[0])
    rank, pivot_row = 0, 0
    for c in range(cols):
        piv = None
        for r in range(pivot_row, rows):
            if m[r][c] != 0:
                piv = r
                break
        if piv is None:
            continue
        m[pivot_row], m[piv] = m[piv], m[pivot_row]
        inv = Fraction(1) / m[pivot_row][c]
        m[pivot_row] = [x * inv for x in m[pivot_row]]
        for r in range(rows):
            if r != pivot_row and m[r][c] != 0:
                f = m[r][c]
                m[r] = [x - f * y for x, y in zip(m[r], m[pivot_row])]
        pivot_row += 1
        rank += 1
    return rank


def r_transpose(a: RMatrix) -> RMatrix:
    return [list(col) for col in zip(*a)]

# 3.  The Descent Theorem, as an executable test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def is_real_pvm(q: Sequence[RMatrix]) -> Tuple[bool, Dict[str, bool]]:
    """Check the three defining identities of a real projection-valued measure."""
    n = len(q[0])
    idem = all(r_mul(qa, qa) == qa for qa in q)
    orth = all(r_mul(q[a], q[b]) == r_zero(n)
               for a in range(len(q)) for b in range(len(q)) if a != b)
    total = r_zero(n)
    for qa in q:
        total = r_add(total, qa)
    complete = total == r_identity(n)
    return (idem and orth and complete,
            {"idempotent": idem, "orthogonal": orth, "complete": complete})


def descent_test(p: Sequence[HMatrix]) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """The certified descent test of the theory.

    Returns the three hypotheses (F), (O), (C), whether the observation is a
    PVM, the observed ranks, and the quantization certificate sum(rank) = n.
    """
    n = len(p[0])
    finite = all(has_finite_entries(pa) for pa in p)
    orth = all(is_infinitesimal_matrix(h_mul(p[a], p[b]))
               for a in range(len(p)) for b in range(len(p)) if a != b)
    complete = approx_eq(h_sum(p, n), h_identity(n))
    observed = [st_matrix(pa) for pa in p]
    is_pvm, parts = is_real_pvm(observed)
    ranks = [r_rank(q) for q in observed]
    return {
        "finite_entries_F": finite,
        "approx_orthogonal_O": orth,
        "approx_complete_C": complete,
        "observation_is_pvm": is_pvm,
        "observation_parts": parts,
        "observed": observed,
        "ranks": ranks,
        "rank_sum": sum(ranks),
        "dimension": n,
        # The Descent Theorem: under (F), (O) and (C) hold iff the observation is a PVM.
        "descent_theorem_confirmed": (not finite) or (is_pvm == (orth and complete)),
    }


def fmt_real_matrix(a: RMatrix) -> str:
    return "[" + "; ".join(" ".join(str(x) for x in row) for row in a) + "]"


def fmt_hyper_matrix(a: HMatrix) -> str:
    return "[" + "; ".join(" , ".join(repr(x) for x in row) for row in a) + "]"


def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)

def demo_eps_channel() -> None:
    banner("1.  The epsilon-channel: an approximate PVM that is NOT an exact one")

    p0 = hyper_matrix([[ONE, EPS], [ZERO, ZERO]])
    p1 = hyper_matrix([[ZERO, ZERO], [ZERO, ONE]])
    p = [p0, p1]

    print("P_1 =", fmt_hyper_matrix(p0))
    print("P_2 =", fmt_hyper_matrix(p1))
    print()
    print("P_1 P_2      =", fmt_hyper_matrix(h_mul(p0, p1)),
          "  (infinitesimal, but NOT zero)")
    print("P_2 P_1      =", fmt_hyper_matrix(h_mul(p1, p0)))
    print("P_1 + P_2    =", fmt_hyper_matrix(h_add(p0, p1)),
          "  (~ I, but NOT equal to I)")

    res = descent_test(p)
    print()
    print("hypothesis (F) finite entries          :", res["finite_entries_F"])
    print("hypothesis (O) approx. orthogonality   :", res["approx_orthogonal_O"])
    print("hypothesis (C) approx. completeness    :", res["approx_complete_C"])
    print("observation is a projection-valued measure:", res["observation_is_pvm"])
    print("   -> observed channels:",
          " and ".join(fmt_real_matrix(q) for q in res["observed"]))

    # Redundancy of idempotency (Theorem: (F)+(O)+(C) => P_a P_a ~ P_a).
    print()
    for a, pa in enumerate(p, start=1):
        print(f"P_{a}^2 ~ P_{a} (idempotency was never assumed):",
              approx_eq(h_mul(pa, pa), pa))

    # Dimension quantization.
    print()
    for a, pa in enumerate(p, start=1):
        print(f"st(tr P_{a}) = {h_trace(pa).st()}  =  rank st(P_{a}) = {res['ranks'][a - 1]}")
    print(f"sum of observed ranks = {res['rank_sum']} = dim = {res['dimension']}")

    # Rigidity: the exact model is the lift of the observation.
    r = [lift(q) for q in res["observed"]]
    n = len(p0)
    exact_idem = all(h_mul(ra, ra) == ra for ra in r)
    exact_orth = h_mul(r[0], r[1]) == h_zero(n) and h_mul(r[1], r[0]) == h_zero(n)
    exact_total = h_sum(r, n) == h_identity(n)
    print()
    print("RIGIDITY.  Exact model R_a = lift(st(P_a)):")
    print("   R exactly idempotent :", exact_idem)
    print("   R exactly orthogonal :", exact_orth)
    print("   R exactly complete   :", exact_total)
    print("   P_a ~ R_a for all a  :", all(approx_eq(pa, ra) for pa, ra in zip(p, r)))
    print("   entrywise difference P_1 - R_1 =",
          fmt_hyper_matrix(h_sub(p[0], r[0])), " (infinitesimal)")

def demo_sharpness_if_direction() -> None:
    banner("2.  Sharpness I: an EXACT hyperreal PVM whose observation is NOT a PVM")

    # P = [[2, w], [-2/w, -1]] is an exact idempotent because w * (-2/w) = -2.
    p0 = hyper_matrix([[Hyper.real(2), W],
                       [Hyper.real(-2) * EPS, Hyper.real(-1)]])
    p1 = h_sub(h_identity(2), p0)
    p = [p0, p1]

    print("P_1 =", fmt_hyper_matrix(p0), "   (contains the infinite entry w)")
    print("P_2 = I - P_1 =", fmt_hyper_matrix(p1))
    print()
    print("P_1^2 = P_1 exactly       :", h_mul(p0, p0) == p0)
    print("P_1 P_2 = 0 exactly       :", h_mul(p0, p1) == h_zero(2))
    print("P_2 P_1 = 0 exactly       :", h_mul(p1, p0) == h_zero(2))
    print("P_1 + P_2 = I exactly     :", h_add(p0, p1) == h_identity(2))
    print("  -> this is an EXACT hyperreal projection-valued measure.")

    res = descent_test(p)
    print()
    print("hypothesis (F) finite entries :", res["finite_entries_F"], " <-- FAILS")
    print("st(P_1) =", fmt_real_matrix(res["observed"][0]))
    q = res["observed"][0]
    print("st(P_1)^2 =", fmt_real_matrix(r_mul(q, q)), " != st(P_1)")
    print("observation is a PVM :", res["observation_is_pvm"], " <-- descent FAILS")
    print()
    print("Mechanism: w * (-2/w) = -2 is an appreciable quantity manufactured from")
    print("an infinite entry and an infinitesimal one.  Entrywise observation sends")
    print("both factors to 0 and loses the contribution.")


def demo_sharpness_only_if_direction() -> None:
    banner("3.  Sharpness II: a PVM observation whose channels are NOT approx. orthogonal")

    p0 = hyper_matrix([[ONE]])
    p1 = hyper_matrix([[W]])
    p = [p0, p1]

    print("P_1 = [1],  P_2 = [w]   (1x1 matrices)")
    print("st(P_1) = [1],  st(P_2) = [0]   -> an honest PVM on R^1")
    res = descent_test(p)
    print("observation is a PVM               :", res["observation_is_pvm"])
    print("P_1 P_2 = [w] is infinitesimal     :", is_infinitesimal_matrix(h_mul(p0, p1)),
          " <-- (O) FAILS badly: w is infinite")
    print("hypothesis (F) finite entries      :", res["finite_entries_F"], " <-- FAILS")
    print()
    print("So without finiteness the 'only if' direction of the Descent Theorem is false.")

def demo_three_channel_quantization() -> None:
    banner("4.  A 4-dimensional, 3-channel approximate PVM: dimension quantization")

    n, half = 4, Fraction(1, 2)
    e2 = EPS * EPS  # 1/w^2, an infinitesimal of higher order

    # Channel 1: rank-2 projection onto span(e1, e2), perturbed infinitesimally.
    p1 = h_zero(n)
    p1[0][0] = ONE
    p1[1][1] = ONE + EPS      # an infinitesimally detuned diagonal entry
    p1[0][2] = EPS
    p1[3][1] = e2

    # Channel 2: rank-1 projection onto span(e3), perturbed.
    p2 = h_zero(n)
    p2[2][2] = ONE
    p2[2][0] = Hyper.real(3) * EPS

    # Channel 3: whatever is needed to make the total exactly I minus a tiny slack.
    p3 = h_sub(h_identity(n), h_add(p1, p2))
    p3[3][3] = p3[3][3] + e2   # extra infinitesimal detuning of the total

    p = [p1, p2, p3]
    res = descent_test(p)

    print("hypothesis (F) finite entries        :", res["finite_entries_F"])
    print("hypothesis (O) approx. orthogonality :", res["approx_orthogonal_O"])
    print("hypothesis (C) approx. completeness  :", res["approx_complete_C"])
    print("observation is a PVM                 :", res["observation_is_pvm"])
    print("Descent Theorem confirmed on this input:", res["descent_theorem_confirmed"])
    print()
    for a in range(3):
        tr_h = h_trace(p[a])
        print(f"channel {a + 1}: hyperreal trace = {tr_h!r:>14}   "
              f"st(trace) = {tr_h.st()}   rank st(P) = {res['ranks'][a]}")
    print(f"\nQUANTIZATION: {' + '.join(str(r) for r in res['ranks'])} "
          f"= {res['rank_sum']} = dim R^{res['dimension']}")
    print("The hyperreal traces live in a continuum; the observed ones are integers.")

def demo_spectral_collapse() -> None:
    banner("5.  Spectral collapse: infinitesimally separated eigenvalues merge")

    # Three rank-1 channels in R^3 with eigenvalues 5, 5 + eps, and -2.
    n = 3
    chans: List[HMatrix] = []
    for i in range(n):
        m = h_zero(n)
        m[i][i] = ONE
        chans.append(m)
    lams = [Hyper.real(5), Hyper.real(5) + EPS, Hyper.real(-2)]

    a = h_zero(n)
    for lam, ch in zip(lams, chans):
        a = h_add(a, h_smul(lam, ch))

    print("eigenvalues:", ", ".join(repr(l) for l in lams))
    print("A = sum_a lambda_a P_a =", fmt_hyper_matrix(a))
    print("st(A) =", fmt_real_matrix(st_matrix(a)))
    print()
    print("observed eigenvalues:", [str(l.st()) for l in lams])
    print("channels 1 and 2 have the SAME observed eigenvalue 5, so they fuse.")

    # Coarse-grain along f: {1,2,3} -> {A, B} merging the two 5-eigenvalue channels.
    f: Callable[[int], str] = lambda i: "A" if i in (0, 1) else "B"
    coarse: Dict[str, RMatrix] = {}
    for i in range(n):
        k = f(i)
        coarse[k] = r_add(coarse.get(k, r_zero(n)), st_matrix(chans[i]))
    mu = {"A": Fraction(5), "B": Fraction(-2)}

    rebuilt = r_zero(n)
    for k, q in coarse.items():
        rebuilt = r_add(rebuilt, [[mu[k] * x for x in row] for row in q])

    print()
    for k in sorted(coarse):
        print(f"coarse channel {k}: eigenvalue {mu[k]}, projection "
              f"{fmt_real_matrix(coarse[k])}, rank {r_rank(coarse[k])}")
    print("sum_k mu_k Q_k =", fmt_real_matrix(rebuilt))
    print("equals st(A):", rebuilt == st_matrix(a))
    print()
    print("The fine 3-channel hyperreal decomposition is observed as a 2-line real one.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 5: Born measure and entropy under coarse-graining
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def born_weight(q: RMatrix, v: Sequence[Fraction]) -> Fraction:
    """p_a = v^T Q_a v."""
    n = len(v)
    qv = [sum((q[i][j] * v[j] for j in range(n)), Fraction(0)) for i in range(n)]
    return sum((v[i] * qv[i] for i in range(n)), Fraction(0))


def eta(t: Fraction) -> float:
    """-t log t, with eta(0) = 0."""
    x = float(t)
    return 0.0 if x <= 0.0 else -x * math.log(x)


def observed_entropy(q: Sequence[RMatrix], v: Sequence[Fraction]) -> float:
    return sum(eta(born_weight(qa, v)) for qa in q)


def coarse_grain(q: Sequence[RMatrix], f: Sequence[int]) -> List[RMatrix]:
    """Merge channels: (f_* Q)_k = sum over {a : f(a) = k} of Q_a."""
    n = len(q[0])
    out: Dict[int, RMatrix] = {}
    for a, qa in enumerate(q):
        out[f[a]] = r_add(out.get(f[a], r_zero(n)), qa)
    return [out[k] for k in sorted(out)]


def demo_entropy() -> None:
    banner("6.  Observed Born measure and entropy monotonicity under coarse-graining")

    # A 4-dimensional PVM with four rank-1 orthogonal channels (diagonal, hence
    # symmetric, so the Born weights are genuine probabilities).
    n = 4
    q: List[RMatrix] = []
    for i in range(n):
        m = r_zero(n)
        m[i][i] = Fraction(1)
        q.append(m)

    ok, parts = is_real_pvm(q)
    print("the fine family is a PVM:", ok, parts)
    print("all channels symmetric  :", all(r_transpose(qa) == qa for qa in q))

    # The exactly normalized state v = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2), giving the uniform
    # Born distribution (1/4, 1/4, 1/4, 1/4).
    v = [Fraction(1, 2)] * 4
    print("\nstate v =", [str(x) for x in v],
          " with |v|^2 =", sum((x * x for x in v), Fraction(0)))
    p = [born_weight(qa, v) for qa in q]
    print("Born weights:", [str(x) for x in p], " sum =", sum(p, Fraction(0)))

    h_fine = observed_entropy(q, v)
    print(f"\nfine entropy   H = {h_fine:.6f}   (= log 4 = {math.log(4):.6f})")

    # (a) merge two channels of positive weight  -> strict decrease
    f_merge = [0, 0, 1, 2]
    qc = coarse_grain(q, f_merge)
    h_c = observed_entropy(qc, v)
    print(f"\n(a) merging channels 1,2 (both weight 1/4 > 0):")
    print(f"    coarse entropy H' = {h_c:.6f}   strict decrease: {h_c < h_fine}")
    print(f"    predicted:  H' = {-0.5 * math.log(0.5) - 2 * 0.25 * math.log(0.25):.6f}")

    # (b) merge a positive-weight channel with a zero-weight channel -> equality
    v2 = [Fraction(1), Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)]
    p2 = [born_weight(qa, v2) for qa in q]
    print(f"\n(b) state v = {[str(x) for x in v2]}, Born weights {[str(x) for x in p2]}")
    h_fine2 = observed_entropy(q, v2)
    h_c2 = observed_entropy(coarse_grain(q, f_merge), v2)
    print(f"    fine H = {h_fine2:.6f},  coarse H' = {h_c2:.6f},  equality: {h_c2 == h_fine2}")
    print("    (equality boundary: no two channels of NONZERO weight were merged)")

    # (c) total merge into one channel -> entropy 0
    f_total = [0, 0, 0, 0]
    h_c3 = observed_entropy(coarse_grain(q, f_total), v)
    print(f"\n(c) merging everything into one channel: H' = {h_c3:.6f} "
          f"(<= {h_fine:.6f}: {h_c3 <= h_fine})")

    # Sharp criterion check across all merging schemes of a 4-element set.
    print("\nSharp equality criterion, checked over all 4^4 merging schemes:")
    bad = 0
    for code in range(4 ** 4):
        f = [(code >> (2 * i)) & 3 for i in range(4)]
        hc = observed_entropy(coarse_grain(q, f), v)
        pw = [born_weight(qa, v) for qa in q]
        no_merge_of_positives = all(
            not (f[a] == f[b] and a != b and pw[a] != 0 and pw[b] != 0)
            for a in range(4) for b in range(4))
        equal = abs(hc - h_fine) < 1e-12
        if equal != no_merge_of_positives:
            bad += 1
    print(f"   schemes violating the criterion: {bad}   (0 means the criterion is exact)")

def demo_functional_calculus() -> None:
    banner("7.  Polynomial functional calculus: st(p(A)) = p(st(A))")

    a = hyper_matrix([[Hyper.real(2) + EPS, Hyper.real(1)],
                      [Hyper.real(-1) * EPS, Hyper.real(3)]])
    print("A =", fmt_hyper_matrix(a), "   (finite entries)")

    # p(X) = X^3 - 2X + 5
    def p_hyper(m: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
        m2 = h_mul(m, m)
        m3 = h_mul(m2, m)
        out = h_sub(m3, h_smul(Hyper.real(2), m))
        return h_add(out, h_smul(Hyper.real(5), h_identity(len(m))))

    def p_real(m: RMatrix) -> RMatrix:
        m2 = r_mul(m, m)
        m3 = r_mul(m2, m)
        out = [[m3[i][j] - 2 * m[i][j] for j in range(len(m))] for i in range(len(m))]
        return r_add(out, [[5 * x for x in row] for row in r_identity(len(m))])

    lhs = st_matrix(p_hyper(a))
    rhs = p_real(st_matrix(a))
    print("p(X) = X^3 - 2X + 5")
    print("st(p(A)) =", fmt_real_matrix(lhs))
    print("p(st A)  =", fmt_real_matrix(rhs))
    print("equal    :", lhs == rhs)

    # Approximate annihilators become exact: B^2 - B is infinitesimal.
    b = hyper_matrix([[ONE, EPS], [ZERO, EPS * EPS]])
    b2mb = h_sub(h_mul(b, b), b)
    print("\nB =", fmt_hyper_matrix(b))
    print("B^2 - B =", fmt_hyper_matrix(b2mb), " infinitesimal:",
          is_infinitesimal_matrix(b2mb))
    sb = st_matrix(b)
    print("st(B) =", fmt_real_matrix(sb), " and st(B)^2 - st(B) = 0 exactly:",
          r_mul(sb, sb) == sb)

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Number = Fraction | int


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  A computable non-Archimedean field: finite Laurent series in omega
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Hyper:
    """A hyperreal number represented as a finite Laurent series in omega.

    ``coeffs`` maps an integer exponent k to the rational coefficient of
    omega**k.  Positive k contributes an infinite part, k = 0 the appreciable
    part, negative k an infinitesimal part.  Zero coefficients are dropped, so
    the representation is canonical and equality is structural.
    """

    coeffs: Tuple[Tuple[int, Fraction], ...]

    # -- construction -------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def of(d: Dict[int, Number]) -> "Hyper":
        cleaned = {k: Fraction(v) for k, v in d.items() if Fraction(v) != 0}
        return Hyper(tuple(sorted(cleaned.items())))

    @staticmethod
    def real(c: Number) -> "Hyper":
        """The image of a real (here: rational) number in the hyperreals."""
        return Hyper.of({0: c})

    @staticmethod
    def omega(power: int = 1) -> "Hyper":
        """omega**power: infinite for power > 0, infinitesimal for power < 0."""
        return Hyper.of({power: 1})

    # -- ring structure -----------------------------------------------------

    def as_dict(self) -> Dict[int, Fraction]:
        return dict(self.coeffs)

    def __add__(self, other: "Hyper") -> "Hyper":
        out = self.as_dict()
        for k, v in other.coeffs:
            out[k] = out.get(k, Fraction(0)) + v
        return Hyper.of(out)

    def __neg__(self) -> "Hyper":
        return Hyper.of({k: -v for k, v in self.coeffs})

    def __sub__(self, other: "Hyper") -> "Hyper":
        return self + (-other)

    def __mul__(self, other: "Hyper") -> "Hyper":
        out: Dict[int, Fraction] = {}
        for k1, v1 in self.coeffs:
            for k2, v2 in other.coeffs:
                out[k1 + k2] = out.get(k1 + k2, Fraction(0)) + v1 * v2
        return Hyper.of(out)

    # -- non-Archimedean predicates ----------------------------------------

    def is_infinite(self) -> bool:
        """True iff some strictly positive power of omega occurs."""
        return any(k > 0 for k, _ in self.coeffs)

    def is_finite(self) -> bool:
        return not self.is_infinite()

    def is_infinitesimal(self) -> bool:
        """True iff every occurring power of omega is strictly negative."""
        return all(k < 0 for k, _ in self.coeffs)

    def st(self) -> Fraction:
        """Standard part: the constant coefficient (0 on infinite elements)."""
        if self.is_infinite():
            return Fraction(0)
        return dict(self.coeffs).get(0, Fraction(0))

    # -- display ------------------------------------------------------------

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        if not self.coeffs:
            return "0"
        pieces: List[str] = []
        for k, v in sorted(self.coeffs, reverse=True):
            mag = "" if abs(v) == 1 and k != 0 else str(abs(v))
            sign = "-" if v < 0 else ""
            if k == 0:
                pieces.append(f"{v}")
            elif k == 1:
                pieces.append(f"{sign}{mag}w")
            elif k == -1:
                pieces.append(f"{sign}{mag or '1'}/w")
            elif k > 0:
                pieces.append(f"{sign}{mag}w^{k}")
            else:
                pieces.append(f"{sign}{mag or '1'}/w^{-k}")
        return " + ".join(pieces).replace("+ -", "- ")


ZERO = Hyper.real(0)
ONE = Hyper.real(1)
W = Hyper.omega(1)        # an infinite element
EPS = Hyper.omega(-1)     # its reciprocal: an infinitesimal

HMatrix = List[List[Hyper]]
RMatrix = List[List[Fraction]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.  Matrix algebra over the hyperreals and over the rationals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def hyper_matrix(rows: Sequence[Sequence[Hyper]]) -> HMatrix:
    return [list(r) for r in rows]


def h_identity(n: int) -> HMatrix:
    return [[ONE if i == j else ZERO for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]


def h_zero(n: int) -> HMatrix:
    return [[ZERO for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]


def h_add(a: HMatrix, b: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    return [[x + y for x, y in zip(ra, rb)] for ra, rb in zip(a, b)]


def h_sub(a: HMatrix, b: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    return [[x - y for x, y in zip(ra, rb)] for ra, rb in zip(a, b)]


def h_mul(a: HMatrix, b: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    n, m, p = len(a), len(b), len(b[0])
    out = [[ZERO for _ in range(p)] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(p):
            acc = ZERO
            for k in range(m):
                acc = acc + a[i][k] * b[k][j]
            out[i][j] = acc
    return out


def h_smul(c: Hyper, a: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    return [[c * x for x in row] for row in a]


def h_sum(mats: Iterable[HMatrix], n: int) -> HMatrix:
    total = h_zero(n)
    for m in mats:
        total = h_add(total, m)
    return total


def h_trace(a: HMatrix) -> Hyper:
    acc = ZERO
    for i in range(len(a)):
        acc = acc + a[i][i]
    return acc


def has_finite_entries(a: HMatrix) -> bool:
    return all(x.is_finite() for row in a for x in row)


def is_infinitesimal_matrix(a: HMatrix) -> bool:
    return all(x.is_infinitesimal() for row in a for x in row)


def approx_eq(a: HMatrix, b: HMatrix) -> bool:
    """A ~ B: the entrywise difference is infinitesimal."""
    return is_infinitesimal_matrix(h_sub(a, b))


def st_matrix(a: HMatrix) -> RMatrix:
    """The observation map: entrywise standard part."""
    return [[x.st() for x in row] for row in a]


def lift(a: RMatrix) -> HMatrix:
    """The canonical lift of a real matrix into the hyperreals."""
    return [[Hyper.real(x) for x in row] for row in a]


def r_identity(n: int) -> RMatrix:
    return [[Fraction(1) if i == j else Fraction(0) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]


def r_mul(a: RMatrix, b: RMatrix) -> RMatrix:
    n, m, p = len(a), len(b), len(b[0])
    return [[sum((a[i][k] * b[k][j] for k in range(m)), Fraction(0)) for j in range(p)]
            for i in range(n)]


def r_add(a: RMatrix, b: RMatrix) -> RMatrix:
    return [[x + y for x, y in zip(ra, rb)] for ra, rb in zip(a, b)]


def r_zero(n: int) -> RMatrix:
    return [[Fraction(0) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]


def r_trace(a: RMatrix) -> Fraction:
    return sum((a[i][i] for i in range(len(a))), Fraction(0))


def r_rank(a: RMatrix) -> int:
    """Exact rank by Gaussian elimination over the rationals."""
    m = [row[:] for row in a]
    rows, cols = len(m), len(m[0])
    rank, pivot_row = 0, 0
    for c in range(cols):
        piv = None
        for r in range(pivot_row, rows):
            if m[r][c] != 0:
                piv = r
                break
        if piv is None:
            continue
        m[pivot_row], m[piv] = m[piv], m[pivot_row]
        inv = Fraction(1) / m[pivot_row][c]
        m[pivot_row] = [x * inv for x in m[pivot_row]]
        for r in range(rows):
            if r != pivot_row and m[r][c] != 0:
                f = m[r][c]
                m[r] = [x - f * y for x, y in zip(m[r], m[pivot_row])]
        pivot_row += 1
        rank += 1
    return rank


def r_transpose(a: RMatrix) -> RMatrix:
    return [list(col) for col in zip(*a)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.  The Descent Theorem, as an executable test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def is_real_pvm(q: Sequence[RMatrix]) -> Tuple[bool, Dict[str, bool]]:
    """Check the three defining identities of a real projection-valued measure."""
    n = len(q[0])
    idem = all(r_mul(qa, qa) == qa for qa in q)
    orth = all(r_mul(q[a], q[b]) == r_zero(n)
               for a in range(len(q)) for b in range(len(q)) if a != b)
    total = r_zero(n)
    for qa in q:
        total = r_add(total, qa)
    complete = total == r_identity(n)
    return (idem and orth and complete,
            {"idempotent": idem, "orthogonal": orth, "complete": complete})


def descent_test(p: Sequence[HMatrix]) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """The certified descent test of the theory.

    Returns the three hypotheses (F), (O), (C), whether the observation is a
    PVM, the observed ranks, and the quantization certificate sum(rank) = n.
    """
    n = len(p[0])
    finite = all(has_finite_entries(pa) for pa in p)
    orth = all(is_infinitesimal_matrix(h_mul(p[a], p[b]))
               for a in range(len(p)) for b in range(len(p)) if a != b)
    complete = approx_eq(h_sum(p, n), h_identity(n))
    observed = [st_matrix(pa) for pa in p]
    is_pvm, parts = is_real_pvm(observed)
    ranks = [r_rank(q) for q in observed]
    return {
        "finite_entries_F": finite,
        "approx_orthogonal_O": orth,
        "approx_complete_C": complete,
        "observation_is_pvm": is_pvm,
        "observation_parts": parts,
        "observed": observed,
        "ranks": ranks,
        "rank_sum": sum(ranks),
        "dimension": n,
        # The Descent Theorem: under (F), (O) and (C) hold iff the observation is a PVM.
        "descent_theorem_confirmed": (not finite) or (is_pvm == (orth and complete)),
    }


def fmt_real_matrix(a: RMatrix) -> str:
    return "[" + "; ".join(" ".join(str(x) for x in row) for row in a) + "]"


def fmt_hyper_matrix(a: HMatrix) -> str:
    return "[" + "; ".join(" , ".join(repr(x) for x in row) for row in a) + "]"


def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)

def demo_eps_channel() -> None:
    banner("1.  The epsilon-channel: an approximate PVM that is NOT an exact one")

    p0 = hyper_matrix([[ONE, EPS], [ZERO, ZERO]])
    p1 = hyper_matrix([[ZERO, ZERO], [ZERO, ONE]])
    p = [p0, p1]

    print("P_1 =", fmt_hyper_matrix(p0))
    print("P_2 =", fmt_hyper_matrix(p1))
    print()
    print("P_1 P_2      =", fmt_hyper_matrix(h_mul(p0, p1)),
          "  (infinitesimal, but NOT zero)")
    print("P_2 P_1      =", fmt_hyper_matrix(h_mul(p1, p0)))
    print("P_1 + P_2    =", fmt_hyper_matrix(h_add(p0, p1)),
          "  (~ I, but NOT equal to I)")

    res = descent_test(p)
    print()
    print("hypothesis (F) finite entries          :", res["finite_entries_F"])
    print("hypothesis (O) approx. orthogonality   :", res["approx_orthogonal_O"])
    print("hypothesis (C) approx. completeness    :", res["approx_complete_C"])
    print("observation is a projection-valued measure:", res["observation_is_pvm"])
    print("   -> observed channels:",
          " and ".join(fmt_real_matrix(q) for q in res["observed"]))

    # Redundancy of idempotency (Theorem: (F)+(O)+(C) => P_a P_a ~ P_a).
    print()
    for a, pa in enumerate(p, start=1):
        print(f"P_{a}^2 ~ P_{a} (idempotency was never assumed):",
              approx_eq(h_mul(pa, pa), pa))

    # Dimension quantization.
    print()
    for a, pa in enumerate(p, start=1):
        print(f"st(tr P_{a}) = {h_trace(pa).st()}  =  rank st(P_{a}) = {res['ranks'][a - 1]}")
    print(f"sum of observed ranks = {res['rank_sum']} = dim = {res['dimension']}")

    # Rigidity: the exact model is the lift of the observation.
    r = [lift(q) for q in res["observed"]]
    n = len(p0)
    exact_idem = all(h_mul(ra, ra) == ra for ra in r)
    exact_orth = h_mul(r[0], r[1]) == h_zero(n) and h_mul(r[1], r[0]) == h_zero(n)
    exact_total = h_sum(r, n) == h_identity(n)
    print()
    print("RIGIDITY.  Exact model R_a = lift(st(P_a)):")
    print("   R exactly idempotent :", exact_idem)
    print("   R exactly orthogonal :", exact_orth)
    print("   R exactly complete   :", exact_total)
    print("   P_a ~ R_a for all a  :", all(approx_eq(pa, ra) for pa, ra in zip(p, r)))
    print("   entrywise difference P_1 - R_1 =",
          fmt_hyper_matrix(h_sub(p[0], r[0])), " (infinitesimal)")

def demo_sharpness_if_direction() -> None:
    banner("2.  Sharpness I: an EXACT hyperreal PVM whose observation is NOT a PVM")

    # P = [[2, w], [-2/w, -1]] is an exact idempotent because w * (-2/w) = -2.
    p0 = hyper_matrix([[Hyper.real(2), W],
                       [Hyper.real(-2) * EPS, Hyper.real(-1)]])
    p1 = h_sub(h_identity(2), p0)
    p = [p0, p1]

    print("P_1 =", fmt_hyper_matrix(p0), "   (contains the infinite entry w)")
    print("P_2 = I - P_1 =", fmt_hyper_matrix(p1))
    print()
    print("P_1^2 = P_1 exactly       :", h_mul(p0, p0) == p0)
    print("P_1 P_2 = 0 exactly       :", h_mul(p0, p1) == h_zero(2))
    print("P_2 P_1 = 0 exactly       :", h_mul(p1, p0) == h_zero(2))
    print("P_1 + P_2 = I exactly     :", h_add(p0, p1) == h_identity(2))
    print("  -> this is an EXACT hyperreal projection-valued measure.")

    res = descent_test(p)
    print()
    print("hypothesis (F) finite entries :", res["finite_entries_F"], " <-- FAILS")
    print("st(P_1) =", fmt_real_matrix(res["observed"][0]))
    q = res["observed"][0]
    print("st(P_1)^2 =", fmt_real_matrix(r_mul(q, q)), " != st(P_1)")
    print("observation is a PVM :", res["observation_is_pvm"], " <-- descent FAILS")
    print()
    print("Mechanism: w * (-2/w) = -2 is an appreciable quantity manufactured from")
    print("an infinite entry and an infinitesimal one.  Entrywise observation sends")
    print("both factors to 0 and loses the contribution.")


def demo_sharpness_only_if_direction() -> None:
    banner("3.  Sharpness II: a PVM observation whose channels are NOT approx. orthogonal")

    p0 = hyper_matrix([[ONE]])
    p1 = hyper_matrix([[W]])
    p = [p0, p1]

    print("P_1 = [1],  P_2 = [w]   (1x1 matrices)")
    print("st(P_1) = [1],  st(P_2) = [0]   -> an honest PVM on R^1")
    res = descent_test(p)
    print("observation is a PVM               :", res["observation_is_pvm"])
    print("P_1 P_2 = [w] is infinitesimal     :", is_infinitesimal_matrix(h_mul(p0, p1)),
          " <-- (O) FAILS badly: w is infinite")
    print("hypothesis (F) finite entries      :", res["finite_entries_F"], " <-- FAILS")
    print()
    print("So without finiteness the 'only if' direction of the Descent Theorem is false.")

def demo_three_channel_quantization() -> None:
    banner("4.  A 4-dimensional, 3-channel approximate PVM: dimension quantization")

    n, half = 4, Fraction(1, 2)
    e2 = EPS * EPS  # 1/w^2, an infinitesimal of higher order

    # Channel 1: rank-2 projection onto span(e1, e2), perturbed infinitesimally.
    p1 = h_zero(n)
    p1[0][0] = ONE
    p1[1][1] = ONE + EPS      # an infinitesimally detuned diagonal entry
    p1[0][2] = EPS
    p1[3][1] = e2

    # Channel 2: rank-1 projection onto span(e3), perturbed.
    p2 = h_zero(n)
    p2[2][2] = ONE
    p2[2][0] = Hyper.real(3) * EPS

    # Channel 3: whatever is needed to make the total exactly I minus a tiny slack.
    p3 = h_sub(h_identity(n), h_add(p1, p2))
    p3[3][3] = p3[3][3] + e2   # extra infinitesimal detuning of the total

    p = [p1, p2, p3]
    res = descent_test(p)

    print("hypothesis (F) finite entries        :", res["finite_entries_F"])
    print("hypothesis (O) approx. orthogonality :", res["approx_orthogonal_O"])
    print("hypothesis (C) approx. completeness  :", res["approx_complete_C"])
    print("observation is a PVM                 :", res["observation_is_pvm"])
    print("Descent Theorem confirmed on this input:", res["descent_theorem_confirmed"])
    print()
    for a in range(3):
        tr_h = h_trace(p[a])
        print(f"channel {a + 1}: hyperreal trace = {tr_h!r:>14}   "
              f"st(trace) = {tr_h.st()}   rank st(P) = {res['ranks'][a]}")
    print(f"\nQUANTIZATION: {' + '.join(str(r) for r in res['ranks'])} "
          f"= {res['rank_sum']} = dim R^{res['dimension']}")
    print("The hyperreal traces live in a continuum; the observed ones are integers.")

def demo_spectral_collapse() -> None:
    banner("5.  Spectral collapse: infinitesimally separated eigenvalues merge")

    # Three rank-1 channels in R^3 with eigenvalues 5, 5 + eps, and -2.
    n = 3
    chans: List[HMatrix] = []
    for i in range(n):
        m = h_zero(n)
        m[i][i] = ONE
        chans.append(m)
    lams = [Hyper.real(5), Hyper.real(5) + EPS, Hyper.real(-2)]

    a = h_zero(n)
    for lam, ch in zip(lams, chans):
        a = h_add(a, h_smul(lam, ch))

    print("eigenvalues:", ", ".join(repr(l) for l in lams))
    print("A = sum_a lambda_a P_a =", fmt_hyper_matrix(a))
    print("st(A) =", fmt_real_matrix(st_matrix(a)))
    print()
    print("observed eigenvalues:", [str(l.st()) for l in lams])
    print("channels 1 and 2 have the SAME observed eigenvalue 5, so they fuse.")

    # Coarse-grain along f: {1,2,3} -> {A, B} merging the two 5-eigenvalue channels.
    f: Callable[[int], str] = lambda i: "A" if i in (0, 1) else "B"
    coarse: Dict[str, RMatrix] = {}
    for i in range(n):
        k = f(i)
        coarse[k] = r_add(coarse.get(k, r_zero(n)), st_matrix(chans[i]))
    mu = {"A": Fraction(5), "B": Fraction(-2)}

    rebuilt = r_zero(n)
    for k, q in coarse.items():
        rebuilt = r_add(rebuilt, [[mu[k] * x for x in row] for row in q])

    print()
    for k in sorted(coarse):
        print(f"coarse channel {k}: eigenvalue {mu[k]}, projection "
              f"{fmt_real_matrix(coarse[k])}, rank {r_rank(coarse[k])}")
    print("sum_k mu_k Q_k =", fmt_real_matrix(rebuilt))
    print("equals st(A):", rebuilt == st_matrix(a))
    print()
    print("The fine 3-channel hyperreal decomposition is observed as a 2-line real one.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 5: Born measure and entropy under coarse-graining
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def born_weight(q: RMatrix, v: Sequence[Fraction]) -> Fraction:
    """p_a = v^T Q_a v."""
    n = len(v)
    qv = [sum((q[i][j] * v[j] for j in range(n)), Fraction(0)) for i in range(n)]
    return sum((v[i] * qv[i] for i in range(n)), Fraction(0))


def eta(t: Fraction) -> float:
    """-t log t, with eta(0) = 0."""
    x = float(t)
    return 0.0 if x <= 0.0 else -x * math.log(x)


def observed_entropy(q: Sequence[RMatrix], v: Sequence[Fraction]) -> float:
    return sum(eta(born_weight(qa, v)) for qa in q)


def coarse_grain(q: Sequence[RMatrix], f: Sequence[int]) -> List[RMatrix]:
    """Merge channels: (f_* Q)_k = sum over {a : f(a) = k} of Q_a."""
    n = len(q[0])
    out: Dict[int, RMatrix] = {}
    for a, qa in enumerate(q):
        out[f[a]] = r_add(out.get(f[a], r_zero(n)), qa)
    return [out[k] for k in sorted(out)]


def demo_entropy() -> None:
    banner("6.  Observed Born measure and entropy monotonicity under coarse-graining")

    # A 4-dimensional PVM with four rank-1 orthogonal channels (diagonal, hence
    # symmetric, so the Born weights are genuine probabilities).
    n = 4
    q: List[RMatrix] = []
    for i in range(n):
        m = r_zero(n)
        m[i][i] = Fraction(1)
        q.append(m)

    ok, parts = is_real_pvm(q)
    print("the fine family is a PVM:", ok, parts)
    print("all channels symmetric  :", all(r_transpose(qa) == qa for qa in q))

    # The exactly normalized state v = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2), giving the uniform
    # Born distribution (1/4, 1/4, 1/4, 1/4).
    v = [Fraction(1, 2)] * 4
    print("\nstate v =", [str(x) for x in v],
          " with |v|^2 =", sum((x * x for x in v), Fraction(0)))
    p = [born_weight(qa, v) for qa in q]
    print("Born weights:", [str(x) for x in p], " sum =", sum(p, Fraction(0)))

    h_fine = observed_entropy(q, v)
    print(f"\nfine entropy   H = {h_fine:.6f}   (= log 4 = {math.log(4):.6f})")

    # (a) merge two channels of positive weight  -> strict decrease
    f_merge = [0, 0, 1, 2]
    qc = coarse_grain(q, f_merge)
    h_c = observed_entropy(qc, v)
    print(f"\n(a) merging channels 1,2 (both weight 1/4 > 0):")
    print(f"    coarse entropy H' = {h_c:.6f}   strict decrease: {h_c < h_fine}")
    print(f"    predicted:  H' = {-0.5 * math.log(0.5) - 2 * 0.25 * math.log(0.25):.6f}")

    # (b) merge a positive-weight channel with a zero-weight channel -> equality
    v2 = [Fraction(1), Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)]
    p2 = [born_weight(qa, v2) for qa in q]
    print(f"\n(b) state v = {[str(x) for x in v2]}, Born weights {[str(x) for x in p2]}")
    h_fine2 = observed_entropy(q, v2)
    h_c2 = observed_entropy(coarse_grain(q, f_merge), v2)
    print(f"    fine H = {h_fine2:.6f},  coarse H' = {h_c2:.6f},  equality: {h_c2 == h_fine2}")
    print("    (equality boundary: no two channels of NONZERO weight were merged)")

    # (c) total merge into one channel -> entropy 0
    f_total = [0, 0, 0, 0]
    h_c3 = observed_entropy(coarse_grain(q, f_total), v)
    print(f"\n(c) merging everything into one channel: H' = {h_c3:.6f} "
          f"(<= {h_fine:.6f}: {h_c3 <= h_fine})")

    # Sharp criterion check across all merging schemes of a 4-element set.
    print("\nSharp equality criterion, checked over all 4^4 merging schemes:")
    bad = 0
    for code in range(4 ** 4):
        f = [(code >> (2 * i)) & 3 for i in range(4)]
        hc = observed_entropy(coarse_grain(q, f), v)
        pw = [born_weight(qa, v) for qa in q]
        no_merge_of_positives = all(
            not (f[a] == f[b] and a != b and pw[a] != 0 and pw[b] != 0)
            for a in range(4) for b in range(4))
        equal = abs(hc - h_fine) < 1e-12
        if equal != no_merge_of_positives:
            bad += 1
    print(f"   schemes violating the criterion: {bad}   (0 means the criterion is exact)")

def demo_functional_calculus() -> None:
    banner("7.  Polynomial functional calculus: st(p(A)) = p(st(A))")

    a = hyper_matrix([[Hyper.real(2) + EPS, Hyper.real(1)],
                      [Hyper.real(-1) * EPS, Hyper.real(3)]])
    print("A =", fmt_hyper_matrix(a), "   (finite entries)")

    # p(X) = X^3 - 2X + 5
    def p_hyper(m: HMatrix) -> HMatrix:
        m2 = h_mul(m, m)
        m3 = h_mul(m2, m)
        out = h_sub(m3, h_smul(Hyper.real(2), m))
        return h_add(out, h_smul(Hyper.real(5), h_identity(len(m))))

    def p_real(m: RMatrix) -> RMatrix:
        m2 = r_mul(m, m)
        m3 = r_mul(m2, m)
        out = [[m3[i][j] - 2 * m[i][j] for j in range(len(m))] for i in range(len(m))]
        return r_add(out, [[5 * x for x in row] for row in r_identity(len(m))])

    lhs = st_matrix(p_hyper(a))
    rhs = p_real(st_matrix(a))
    print("p(X) = X^3 - 2X + 5")
    print("st(p(A)) =", fmt_real_matrix(lhs))
    print("p(st A)  =", fmt_real_matrix(rhs))
    print("equal    :", lhs == rhs)

    # Approximate annihilators become exact: B^2 - B is infinitesimal.
    b = hyper_matrix([[ONE, EPS], [ZERO, EPS * EPS]])
    b2mb = h_sub(h_mul(b, b), b)
    print("\nB =", fmt_hyper_matrix(b))
    print("B^2 - B =", fmt_hyper_matrix(b2mb), " infinitesimal:",
          is_infinitesimal_matrix(b2mb))
    sb = st_matrix(b)
    print("st(B) =", fmt_real_matrix(sb), " and st(B)^2 - st(B) = 0 exactly:",
          r_mul(sb, sb) == sb)
